first.rationale:
Both live symptoms (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and onboarding completion is plausibly upstream of the activation drop, so a single onboarding intervention has the widest leverage on the one available slot. I intend simplify_onboarding, grounded in memory_86 and memory_31. Verification triage: I spend the budget on the two beliefs that are simultaneously most decision-consequential and least supported for the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. (1) memory_86 directly underwrites my intended action, but as recorded it was validated only on completion rate and time-to-value /revrevenue proxies; shortening onboarding can lift completion while stripping out the qualification and value-setup steps that make later revenue durable, so I need the original record to see whether qualified revenue or retention was ever measured. (2) memory_73 is the loudest competing pull given the competitor's entry pricing, and it is the highest-regret path if wrong: an acquisition/revenue lift record says nothing about margin, discount-cohort retention, or whether the acquired accounts were qualified, and price cuts are hard to unwind. I deliberately do not spend budget on memory_57, memory_44, or memory_91: referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist do not address the observed funnel regression, and memory_91 is a plausible fallback rather than the belief I am about to act on. Downstream value risk is explicit: reducing required fields or steps may degrade lead qualification and routing, converting a completion-rate win into lower-quality pipeline. I therefore run it as a small guarded test with a holdout, with qualified pipeline per signup and 30-day retention as guardrail metrics rather than completion alone, and I treat the inherited claims as directionally credible but not yet established against the revenue objective 
ull. If the archive shows memory_86 rested only on proxy metrics, I will keep the test small and hold activation_messaging (memory_91) as the lower-risk alternative; if it shows promotional pricing durably added qualified revenue, that changes the ranking.

final.rationale: The archive resolved both questions in the direction that settles the decision. exp_86 shows the onboarding shortening lifted not just the proxy (completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days) but also 30-day retention +3%, which is the durability signal I was worried was missing; my main objection to acting on memory_86 is answered. exp_73 is the opposite: signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% are real, but 30-day retention -12% means the discounted cohort does not survive the first renewal cycle, and the original record explicitly warns against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. So the competitor's entry pricing must NOT be answered with promotional_pricing under a long-term qualified-revenue objective; matching them would buy a quarter of signups and hand back the revenue at renewal. Choosing simplify_onboarding: it targets the observed -4% onboarding completion regression directly and plausibly the -6% activation drop upstream of it, it is corroborated by two independent records (exp_86 on completion and retention, memory_31 on SMB first-week activation), and it is the only candidate with verified positive retention. It also happens to be a defensible non-price response to a price attacker, since faster time-to-value raises switching cost. Scale moves from small_guarded_test to standard_experiment because the retention guardrail that justified extra caution has now been checked rather than assumed. Remaining uncertainty I am not papering over: exp_86 measured retention at 30 days, not qualified revenue or pipeline quality, and the two experiments' onboarding flows may differ from the current one, so lead-qualification degradation is still a live downstream risk. I therefore instrument qualified pipeline per signup and lead-routing accuracy as guardrails alongside completion and activation, keep a holdout, and pre-commit to rolling back if qualified pipeline per signup falls even while completion rises. activation_messaging (memory_91) stays the fallback if the onboarding test shows funnel-quality erosion; referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist remain unverified and do not address this quarter's regression.
